item.text: {"question_id":"1B.8","answer":"The 8 January 2023 crisis provides mixed, contested evidence. Lula directly ordered federal intervention in Federal District security, rejected a proposed GLO, called for punishment regardless of rank, and publicly acknowledged a serious intelligence failure; he also ordered a review of approximately 2,000 secrecy appeals through CGU procedures (BATCH-0009-E010, BATCH-0018-E010, BATCH-0018-E008). Operational accounts indicate that the Plan Escudo was activated before the attack, that the GSI chief contacted Lula and sought urgent military reinforcement, and that the Planalto was evacuated and invasions contained without deaths; the GSI chief also stated that he independently ordered an inquiry into failures and later changed personnel (BATCH-0020-E019, BATCH-0020-E020, BATCH-0020-E023, BATCH-0020-E028, BATCH-0020-E031). A Ministry of Justice account further states that legal constraints limited National Force deployment without Federal District consent, that an arrangement had assigned the Force to specified federal sites, and that intervention later created unified command; it also says camera preservation followed a pre-existing 30-day contractual retention practice and preserved records considered important to investigations (BATCH-0020-E017, BATCH-0020-E018). Against this, testimony and opposition accounts allege that formal intelligence channels were not used, sensitive information was exchanged through personal WhatsApp, the integrated protocol or crisis center and a detailed police operations plan were not activated, warnings and reinforcement opportunities were inadequately acted upon, and some images were unavailable or deleted under disputed retention practices (BATCH-0020-E021, BATCH-0020-E022, BATCH-0020-E024, BATCH-0020-E025, BATCH-0020-E026). The record also indicates inherited personnel and institutional constraints, including the GSI chief’s account that many officials and structures were carried over from the prior government and that he initially changed only a small number of personnel before broader changes after the crisis (BATCH-0020-E023). Lula’s personal operational direction is established for the federal intervention, GLO decision, public accountability stance, and CGU review, but not for most security-system failures, reinforcement timing, image-retention practices, or the GSI chief’s inquiry and personnel decisions. The supplied inquiry material is testimonial and politically contested, and does not establish a final independent finding that Lula personally caused or corrected the procedural
